pathway.title: Xerox Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The revenue base is recurring but shrinking: post sale revenue is 70% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026, yet pro forma revenue fell 5.0% after falling 7.6% in 2025, and equipment gross margin fell to 5.0% in the third quarter from 26.1%, so scale protects cash flow less each year. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–69; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Earnings are thin and flattered by one-offs: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 621 million, 8.10% of revenue, includes about USD 205 million of gains from debt repurchases and tariff refunds, so the underlying figure is about USD 416 million, or 5.43% of revenue, and the issuer states no EBITDA of its own. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11

- Leverage is high on any basis: total debt is 6.80x EBITDA and 10.14x without the one-offs, the issuer's target below 3.0x would need EBITDA of about USD 1,407 million, which is 2.27x today's level, and net debt of USD 3,810 million, or 6.14x, becomes USD 3,756 million, or 6.05x, pro forma for the exchange expected on or about November 13, 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C7; calculation C8

- Interest absorbs most of the earnings base: non-financing interest was USD 357 million in the last twelve months, 57.49% of reported EBITDA and 85.82% of the underlying figure, and the stated coupons on today's debt come to at least USD 350 million a year, with recent secured and parent notes at 10.25% to 13.50%. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 216–220; calculation C3; calculation C4

- Free cash flow cannot delever the company: operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 37 million in the last twelve months, operating cash flow includes USD 265 million of net finance receivable sale proceeds that are shrinking, and the 2026 operating cash flow outlook was cut to USD 145 million to USD 195 million from about USD 340 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 205; calculation C6

- Liquidity is adequate through 2027 and not beyond: cash of USD 410 million, with pro forma cash for the exchange not established, and net revolver availability of USD 225 million total USD 635 million, 2.93x the USD 217 million due through 2027 but only 0.66x the USD 969 million due through 2028, and the revolver matures no later than May 22, 2028. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C2

- Refinancing capacity is the central weakness: USD 2,931 million, 67.41% of principal, falls due in 2028 to 2030, new money has cost 10.25% to 13.50%, and the secured debt tests, a limit of USD 2.0 billion and a first lien leverage test, leave headroom that cannot be sized from the supplied documents, so refinancing is likely to need more asset-backed or priority shifting transactions. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C1; calculation C9

- Financial policy is moving the right way through steps that shift priority: dividends are being suspended to save about USD 28 million a year and notes were bought back at 50.5% of par, but the Joint Venture and the exchange put assets and first lien claims ahead of unsecured creditors, and the exchange raises annual coupon cost by USD 2.73 million while cutting principal by USD 54 million. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C5

- The cushion under creditors has gone: goodwill impairments of USD 1,058 million in 2024 and USD 959 million in 2026 and an equity deficit of USD 492 million at Xerox Corporation, plus pension and retiree medical liabilities of USD 1,135 million outside total debt, leave value support resting on cash flow and on collateral that the supplied documents do not value. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; calculation C12

runs.text: - Recurring post sale revenue is the main strength: post sale revenue of USD 3,955 million is 70% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the customer base is broad, with no dependence on a single customer. Supplies, service and rentals follow the installed equipment base, so cash flow keeps arriving through a mild downturn, which supports debt service in the next year but not the 2028 maturities. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69

- Cost and synergy delivery is lifting profit: adjusted operating income was USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million pro forma a year earlier, selling, administrative and general expense fell to 20.0% of third quarter revenue from 24.3%, and more than USD 300 million of run-rate synergies are targeted by the end of 2027. Because costs fall without revenue growth, EBITDA can rise even as sales decline, which is the main route to lower leverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7

- Financial policy now favors creditors in direction: dividends are suspended from January 2027 to save about USD 28 million a year, distributions to the parent fell to USD 45 million in nine months, and notes were retired at 50.5% of par. Cash stays in the group and debt falls cheaply, which slows net debt growth, although the structures used also shift priority. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C13

- Near-term liquidity is adequate: cash of USD 410 million and net revolver availability of USD 225 million total USD 635 million against USD 217 million due through 2027, and no single year before 2028 has maturities above USD 197 million. There is no forced refinancing for about 18 months, which gives time to deliver the savings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C2

- The largest weakness is the 2028 to 2030 maturity wall: USD 2,931 million, 67.41% of principal, falls due against USD 621 million of EBITDA and USD 37 million of free cash flow. Repayment can only come from refinancing, and the revolver matures no later than May 22, 2028, so the committed liquidity line ends before the largest maturities. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C15

- Earnings are thin and flattered: EBITDA of USD 621 million includes about USD 205 million of one-off gains, and interest of USD 357 million over twelve months takes 85.82% of the underlying USD 416 million. Little remains for debt service, and leverage is 10.14x on the underlying figure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C10; calculation C11

- Free cash flow is weak and propped by asset sales: operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 37 million, and USD 265 million of finance receivable sale proceeds, down from USD 752 million in 2024 to USD 357 million in 2025, sit inside operating cash flow. The funding source is shrinking, and the 2026 outlook was cut to USD 145 million to USD 195 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 205; calculation C6

- Revenue and equipment margin are under pressure: pro forma revenue fell 5.0% in nine months and equipment gross margin was 5.0% in the third quarter against 26.1%, with product cost increases and mix cited. Shrinking installed base and weak equipment profit erode the post sale annuity over time, so the savings must outrun the decline. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–69; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84

- Priority-shifting financings and negative equity weaken unsecured creditors: the Joint Venture put the brand behind USD 450 million of limited-recourse debt, the exchange adds USD 120 million of first lien notes, and Xerox Corporation's equity is a deficit of USD 492 million after USD 2,017 million of goodwill impairments. Further steps of this kind would lower unsecured recovery even as total debt falls. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C12

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Xerox Corporation completed the acquisition of Lexmark from Ninestar Group Company Limited on July 1, 2025 for total consideration of USD 749 million after a USD 19 million working capital reduction. It was financed mainly with new debt: second lien notes of USD 500 million in total, released from escrow at closing, and 13.00% notes of the parent of USD 250 million due 2030, while the USD 400 million of first lien notes issued in April 2025 mainly redeemed a parent note that matured in 2025. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_xrx-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 218; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 219; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 220; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C17

On February 17, 2026 Xerox Corporation contributed the Xerox brand trademarks and related intellectual property to a new entity, XRX Brandco Holdings LLC, whose term loans of USD 405 million and Class A Units of USD 45 million were funded by investors including funds managed by Angelo, Gordon & Co., L.P. After USD 46 million of closing costs the net proceeds were USD 404 million, distributed to Xerox Corporation for general corporate purposes. The group pays the entity a royalty of 2.0% of specified revenue, and both instruments amortize by 4.50% of the closing amount each quarter after September 30, 2026, so the USD 450 million counted as debt falls by USD 81 million a year before a final payment. The entity's creditors have recourse to its assets and to the guarantees and collateral support in the licence agreement, but not to the general credit of Xerox Corporation or Xerox Holdings Corporation. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_xrx-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 8–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C12; calculation C21

In October 2026 the company agreed an exchange with certain holders of Xerox Holdings Corporation's 5.50% notes due 2028: about USD 174 million of those notes for about USD 120 million of new 10.25% first lien senior secured notes due 2030 of Xerox Corporation, about 3.9 million shares of common stock and accrued interest in cash. It was expected to close on or about November 13, 2026, would cut debt by up to USD 54 million and would move USD 120 million of maturity from 2028 to 2030, but the new notes rank ahead of the unsecured and second lien debt of Xerox Corporation, and completion is not confirmed in the supplied documents. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C15; Source readiness (CP-0)

Other funding actions in 2026 are the sale of rights to tariff refund receivables carrying USD 105 million for about USD 80 million, treated as financing with imputed interest of about USD 25 million; repurchases of USD 194 million of the parent's 2028 notes and USD 6 million of second lien notes for about USD 101 million; continued sales of finance receivables to funding partners, with net proceeds of USD 122 million in the first nine months; and Amendment No. 2 to the First Lien Term Loan Credit Agreement, filed with a current report dated October 29, 2026, whose terms are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox Corporation carries USD 4,220 million of debt at September 30, 2026, 6.80x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 621 million, so creditors depend on a thin and volatile earnings base. fields.value: Leverage on the issuer's own statements is high and unstable: total debt of USD 4,220 million is 6.80x derived EBITDA for the last twelve months, against 41.23x in FY2025 and 14.16x in FY2024, because EBITDA fell to USD 103 million in FY2025 after Lexmark purchase accounting and restructuring charges and recovered to USD 621 million as those charges eased, helped by about USD 205 million of one-off gains in 2026 from debt repurchases and tariff refunds. The mechanism is that debt rose with the Lexmark acquisition while the earnings base stayed thin, so a small shortfall in EBITDA moves the ratio by several turns; the exchange expected in November 2026 would cut principal by up to about USD 54 million, which changes the ratio by less than 0.1x. That target needs EBITDA of about USD 1,407 million on today's debt, so the gap is large even if the one-off gains prove to be a timing effect; what would change the view is confirmed debt reduction well beyond the exchange or an issuer-stated EBITDA that differs materially from the derived figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of Xerox Corp (issuer-108772), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the group's business, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation behaviour and the transactions that affect creditors of Xerox Corporation, built from the five supplied filings and the source readiness review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox Corp is a shrinking print business whose parent has cut shareholder payouts and made debt reduction its priority, but recent financings that ring-fenced the brand and added secured debt keep governance risk at Medium for creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is identified: Xerox Holdings Corporation owns all of the shares of Xerox Corporation and is itself publicly held, so creditors depend on the parent's choices on distributions, guarantees and exchanges. Xerox Corporation sent USD 45 million to the parent in the first nine months of 2026 while its own equity fell to a deficit of USD 492 million, and the proxy statement that would show the board and large holders is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 255; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business is a large print annuity that is shrinking: post sale revenue is 70% of revenue and Print and Other produces 91% of it in the first nine months of 2026, but pro forma revenue fell 5.0% in that period after falling 7.6% in 2025, so earnings recovery rests on cost savings rather than growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 65–67; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Profitability is recovering from a low base through integration savings and cost discipline, with adjusted operating income of USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million a year earlier on a pro forma basis, yet the gain sits in Print and Other, with segment profit of USD 443 million, while IT Solutions earned USD 21 million and corporate costs took USD 65 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Asset-value support is weaker than the earnings recovery suggests, because the Print and Other business has been written down twice in two years: goodwill impairments of USD 1,058 million in the third quarter of 2024 and USD 959 million in the third quarter of 2026, together USD 2,017 million, the latest driven by lower projections and rising memory prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The structure puts all group debt on Xerox Corporation: it guarantees the parent's notes and received the proceeds in full, so its balance sheet debt of USD 4,220 million equals the group total, of which USD 1,676 million is owed to the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 100; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership is simple and shows no sponsor on the evidence supplied: the parent is listed on Nasdaq and has an 8% cumulative Series A preferred stock of USD 180 million liquidation value, and the only sponsor-type event in the record is the 2023 purchase of shares from Carl C. Icahn and his affiliates, equal to 21.98% of the common shares outstanding at the end of 2022, for USD 542 million, funded with a USD 555 million credit agreement that the term loan B later refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 252; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 254; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The group has cut shareholder payouts hard, which supports creditors: common dividends declared fell from USD 146 million in 2023 to USD 27 million in 2025, the annual rate per share went from USD 1.00 to USD 0.10 during 2025, and the Board suspended common and preferred dividends from January 2027 to conserve about USD 28 million a year, although the USD 14 million annual preferred dividend keeps accumulating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash still moves up to the parent even as the issuer's own equity has turned negative: Xerox Corporation distributed USD 722 million to Xerox Holdings Corporation in 2023, USD 202 million in 2024, USD 79 million in 2025 and USD 45 million in the first nine months of 2026, and its equity swung from USD 629 million at the end of 2025 to a deficit of USD 492 million at September 30, 2026. The amounts are shrinking, but the limits that the debt documents place on such distributions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Joint Venture and the first lien exchange move assets or priority ahead of other creditors, even though each reduces debt or raises cash: in February 2026 the Xerox brand trademarks went into a ring-fenced entity that raised USD 405 million of term loans and USD 45 million of redeemable units with limited recourse to the group and amortization of USD 81 million a year from late 2026, and the October 2026 exchange would swap USD 174 million of the parent's 2028 notes for about USD 120 million of new first lien notes of Xerox Corporation plus shares, cutting debt by up to USD 54 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_xrx-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C12; calculation C15; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity actions are being taken at a discount and the funding they provided is shrinking: repurchases retired USD 200 million of notes for about USD 101 million, which cut debt cheaply, but a USD 105 million tariff refund claim was sold for about USD 80 million, and net proceeds from finance receivable sales fell from USD 752 million in 2024 to USD 357 million in 2025 and USD 122 million in the first nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Controls and reporting are adequate but not clean: the auditor gave unqualified opinions and found internal control effective at the end of 2025, with Lexmark, 13% of assets and 14% of revenue, excluded from that assessment, and errors in Lexmark's opening balance sheet had to be corrected, cutting receivables by USD 81 million and adding USD 41 million to goodwill, which the company judged immaterial.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management turnover and supplier dependence add execution risk: four of the six executive officers took their present roles in 2025, an offer letter to the President and Chief Operating Officer and a release agreement with the Chief Executive Officer are both dated March 31, 2026 with the current report carrying them not supplied, and FUJIFILM Business Innovation supplied products worth USD 811 million in 2025, 11.55% of revenue.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium risk level is that behaviour has turned creditor-friendly: dividends are being suspended, debt reduction is the stated first priority with a target below 3.0x total debt to EBITDA, notes were repurchased at 50.5% of par, adjusted operating income has grown year over year for three consecutive quarters, and no sponsor is taking fees or recapitalising the company. The Joint Venture lenders also have no recourse to the general credit of Xerox Corporation or the parent beyond the contracted support, and warrants exercised with notes retired about USD 8 million of convertible notes in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to Low if the exchange closes as described, further discounted repurchases follow, the proxy statement shows an independent board with no large holder able to direct payouts, and the executed documents show tight limits on distributions and asset transfers. It would move to High if further brand or asset financings, first lien issuance or distributions to the parent continue while operating cash flow stays near the lowered outlook of USD 145 million to USD 195 million for 2026, or if the legal documents show that the Joint Venture support obligations limit recovery for unsecured creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox Corporation completed the acquisition of Lexmark from Ninestar Group Company Limited on July 1, 2025 for total consideration of USD 749 million after a USD 19 million working capital reduction. It was financed mainly with new debt: second lien notes of USD 500 million in total, released from escrow at closing, and 13.00% notes of the parent of USD 250 million due 2030, while the USD 400 million of first lien notes issued in April 2025 mainly redeemed a parent note that matured in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On February 17, 2026 Xerox Corporation contributed the Xerox brand trademarks and related intellectual property to a new entity, XRX Brandco Holdings LLC, whose term loans of USD 405 million and Class A Units of USD 45 million were funded by investors including funds managed by Angelo, Gordon & Co., L.P. After USD 46 million of closing costs the net proceeds were USD 404 million, distributed to Xerox Corporation for general corporate purposes. The group pays the entity a royalty of 2.0% of specified revenue, and both instruments amortize by 4.50% of the closing amount each quarter after September 30, 2026, so the USD 450 million counted as debt falls by USD 81 million a year before a final payment. The entity's creditors have recourse to its assets and to the guarantees and collateral support in the licence agreement, but not to the general credit of Xerox Corporation or Xerox Holdings Corporation.

fields.value: In October 2026 the company agreed an exchange with certain holders of Xerox Holdings Corporation's 5.50% notes due 2028: about USD 174 million of those notes for about USD 120 million of new 10.25% first lien senior secured notes due 2030 of Xerox Corporation, about 3.9 million shares of common stock and accrued interest in cash. It was expected to close on or about November 13, 2026, would cut debt by up to USD 54 million and would move USD 120 million of maturity from 2028 to 2030, but the new notes rank ahead of the unsecured and second lien debt of Xerox Corporation, and completion is not confirmed in the supplied documents.

It is driven by financings that moved the brand and added first lien debt ahead of other creditors, because those steps shift priority and collateral away from unsecured and second lien creditors, which implies lower recovery for them even though total debt is falling. The countervailing evidence is that no sponsor is identified, dividends are being suspended and each step was disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Xerox Corp (issuer-108772), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business risk, financial profile, refinancing capacity and the primary downside path of Xerox Corporation, built from the five supplied filings and the three earlier modules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox Corp presents weak fundamental credit quality: a shrinking print business supports USD 4,220 million of debt at 6.80x last-twelve-months EBITDA, and about USD 2,931 million falls due in 2028 to 2030, so creditors rely on refinancing, not free cash flow.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C1

fields.value: That EBITDA of USD 621 million includes about USD 205 million of one-off gains; without them leverage is 10.14x, interest on the debt stack takes at least USD 350 million a year and free cash flow was USD 37 million. Net debt of USD 3,810 million at September 30, 2026 would be USD 3,756 million pro forma for the exchange expected on or about November 13, 2026, or 6.05x against 6.14x, but closing is not confirmed. Cash of USD 410 million, with pro forma cash not established, and net revolver availability of USD 225 million cover the 2027 maturities, not 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings are thin and flattered by one-offs: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 621 million, 8.10% of revenue, includes about USD 205 million of gains from debt repurchases and tariff refunds, so the underlying figure is about USD 416 million, or 5.43% of revenue, and the issuer states no EBITDA of its own.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.value: - Leverage is high on any basis: total debt is 6.80x EBITDA and 10.14x without the one-offs, the issuer's target below 3.0x would need EBITDA of about USD 1,407 million, which is 2.27x today's level, and net debt of USD 3,810 million, or 6.14x, becomes USD 3,756 million, or 6.05x, pro forma for the exchange expected on or about November 13, 2026.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest absorbs most of the earnings base: non-financing interest was USD 357 million in the last twelve months, 57.49% of reported EBITDA and 85.82% of the underlying figure, and the stated coupons on today's debt come to at least USD 350 million a year, with recent secured and parent notes at 10.25% to 13.50%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 216–220; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.value: - Free cash flow cannot delever the company: operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 37 million in the last twelve months, operating cash flow includes USD 265 million of net finance receivable sale proceeds that are shrinking, and the 2026 operating cash flow outlook was cut to USD 145 million to USD 195 million from about USD 340 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 205; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate through 2027 and not beyond: cash of USD 410 million, with pro forma cash for the exchange not established, and net revolver availability of USD 225 million total USD 635 million, 2.93x the USD 217 million due through 2027 but only 0.66x the USD 969 million due through 2028, and the revolver matures no later than May 22, 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing capacity is the central weakness: USD 2,931 million, 67.41% of principal, falls due in 2028 to 2030, new money has cost 10.25% to 13.50%, and the secured debt tests, a limit of USD 2.0 billion and a first lien leverage test, leave headroom that cannot be sized from the supplied documents, so refinancing is likely to need more asset-backed or priority shifting transactions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C1; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is moving the right way through steps that shift priority: dividends are being suspended to save about USD 28 million a year and notes were bought back at 50.5% of par, but the Joint Venture and the exchange put assets and first lien claims ahead of unsecured creditors, and the exchange raises annual coupon cost by USD 2.73 million while cutting principal by USD 54 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cushion under creditors has gone: goodwill impairments of USD 1,058 million in 2024 and USD 959 million in 2026 and an equity deficit of USD 492 million at Xerox Corporation, plus pension and retiree medical liabilities of USD 1,135 million outside total debt, leave value support resting on cash flow and on collateral that the supplied documents do not value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak assessment is operating momentum and a near-term cushion: adjusted operating income grew year over year for three consecutive quarters to USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million pro forma, cost savings of more than USD 500 million were reached by the end of 2025, the Lexmark synergy target is more than USD 300 million by the end of 2027, no maturity above USD 197 million falls due before 2028, and the dividend suspension, discounted repurchases and the exchange all reduce debt. If those synergies land on revenue that stabilizes, EBITDA could move well above the underlying USD 416 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve to adequate if pro forma revenue stabilizes, underlying EBITDA rises toward the reported USD 621 million with operating cash flow above the USD 195 million top of the outlook, and the maturities due from 2028 are refinanced or exchanged at lower cost without further priority shifting. It would worsen if the outlook is cut again, receivable sale proceeds keep falling, net revolver availability falls below USD 225 million, or the exchange does not close and the 2028 notes stay at USD 556 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA, so every leverage and cover figure rests on a derived measure that adds back the goodwill impairment and keeps USD 205 million of one-off gains, and the choice moves leverage by 3.34x, which could move the weak assessment of earnings either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, market price or covenant compliance figure is supplied, so refinancing capacity rests on the coupons of recent issues and on company statements; actual market access and covenant headroom could be better or worse than the weak assessment of refinancing assumes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The company gives an outlook for 2026 operating cash flow only, with no 2027 guidance or forecast, so the downside path is qualitative and its timing rests on the maturity ladder and the revolver maturity rather than on a cash flow projection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The amended Term Loan B amortization is not supplied, so the USD 197 million due in 2027 is taken from the company's own ladder and could be higher or lower, which would change how long the USD 635 million of liquidity lasts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Recurring post sale revenue is the main strength: post sale revenue of USD 3,955 million is 70% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the customer base is broad, with no dependence on a single customer. Supplies, service and rentals follow the installed equipment base, so cash flow keeps arriving through a mild downturn, which supports debt service in the next year but not the 2028 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost and synergy delivery is lifting profit: adjusted operating income was USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million pro forma a year earlier, selling, administrative and general expense fell to 20.0% of third quarter revenue from 24.3%, and more than USD 300 million of run-rate synergies are targeted by the end of 2027. Because costs fall without revenue growth, EBITDA can rise even as sales decline, which is the main route to lower leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy now favors creditors in direction: dividends are suspended from January 2027 to save about USD 28 million a year, distributions to the parent fell to USD 45 million in nine months, and notes were retired at 50.5% of par. Cash stays in the group and debt falls cheaply, which slows net debt growth, although the structures used also shift priority.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Near-term liquidity is adequate: cash of USD 410 million and net revolver availability of USD 225 million total USD 635 million against USD 217 million due through 2027, and no single year before 2028 has maturities above USD 197 million. There is no forced refinancing for about 18 months, which gives time to deliver the savings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The largest weakness is the 2028 to 2030 maturity wall: USD 2,931 million, 67.41% of principal, falls due against USD 621 million of EBITDA and USD 37 million of free cash flow. Repayment can only come from refinancing, and the revolver matures no later than May 22, 2028, so the committed liquidity line ends before the largest maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings are thin and flattered: EBITDA of USD 621 million includes about USD 205 million of one-off gains, and interest of USD 357 million over twelve months takes 85.82% of the underlying USD 416 million. Little remains for debt service, and leverage is 10.14x on the underlying figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow is weak and propped by asset sales: operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 37 million, and USD 265 million of finance receivable sale proceeds, down from USD 752 million in 2024 to USD 357 million in 2025, sit inside operating cash flow. The funding source is shrinking, and the 2026 outlook was cut to USD 145 million to USD 195 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 205; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue and equipment margin are under pressure: pro forma revenue fell 5.0% in nine months and equipment gross margin was 5.0% in the third quarter against 26.1%, with product cost increases and mix cited. Shrinking installed base and weak equipment profit erode the post sale annuity over time, so the savings must outrun the decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Priority-shifting financings and negative equity weaken unsecured creditors: the Joint Venture put the brand behind USD 450 million of limited-recourse debt, the exchange adds USD 120 million of first lien notes, and Xerox Corporation's equity is a deficit of USD 492 million after USD 2,017 million of goodwill impairments. Further steps of this kind would lower unsecured recovery even as total debt falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox sells printing equipment, supplies and managed print services, finances equipment through Xerox Financial Services, and since the 2024 purchase of ITsavvy sells IT infrastructure solutions; Print and Other is 91% of nine-month 2026 revenue and IT Solutions 9%, and 43% of 2025 revenue came from outside the United States. The model supports cash flow visibility because 70% of revenue is post sale and customers are diverse, but it weakens refinancing confidence because reported growth of 12.86% in the first nine months of 2026 comes from adding Lexmark for six more months while pro forma revenue fell 5.0%, so the base that services the debt is shrinking.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox Corporation is wholly owned by Xerox Holdings Corporation, a Nasdaq-listed parent with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, and it carries all group debt because it guarantees the parent's notes and receives the proceeds in full. Creditors therefore depend on parent choices: distributions fell to USD 45 million in the first nine months of 2026 and dividends are being suspended, but the Joint Venture and the exchange show a willingness to move assets and priority, which keeps governance risk at Medium; board and holder detail is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring in structure and declining in direction: post sale revenue of USD 3,955 million fell 4.1% pro forma in the first nine months of 2026, equipment sales rose 2.6% in the third quarter with installations up 9.0% but at a gross margin of 5.0%, IT Solutions fell 18.9% on the timing of large prior-year public sector placements, and financing revenue fell 22.5% as receivables are sold. Pricing power is limited because the company competes on price with Brother, Canon, FUJIFILM Business Innovation, HP, Konica Minolta, Kyocera and Ricoh and cites product cost increases and mix against gross margin, so revenue is best described as recurring, cyclical and structurally declining.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are being rebuilt through cost actions rather than pricing: selling, administrative and general expense fell to 20.0% of third quarter revenue from 24.3%, research and development to 3.0% from 3.8%, and total gross margin rose to 29.2% from 22.7%. About 1.8 percentage points of the nine-month gross margin of 31.6% came from tariff receivables that will not repeat, and equipment gross margin of 5.0%, which the company also attributes in part to non-recurring prior-year purchase accounting adjustments, shows exposure to input costs, since the company lowered its Print and Other projections on sustained memory price increases. Margins can be defended against volume pressure only if the savings continue, because restructuring cost USD 82 million in the first nine months and the workforce reduction announced in October 2025 is still being carried out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low and conversion is poor: capital expenditure was USD 94 million over the last twelve months, 1.23% of revenue, but operating cash flow of USD 131 million after interest, restructuring payments of USD 60 million and retirement plan contributions of USD 118 million in the first nine months of 2026 left USD 37 million, and the operating cash flow includes USD 265 million of net finance receivable sale proceeds. EBITDA therefore does not translate into free cash flow for deleveraging, and capital expenditure is too small a lever to change that over the maturity wall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is the force that matters: seven named print competitors compete on technology, price, service and brand, so equipment pricing cannot absorb product cost increases, which shows in the 5.0% equipment gross margin and caps margin recovery. Supplier power is concentrated in FUJIFILM Business Innovation, the largest sourcing partner, with purchases of USD 811 million in 2025 or 11.55% of revenue, so a supply dispute would interrupt equipment and parts at once. Buyer power is moderate because no customer is significant, and entry and substitution threats come mainly from digital workflows and hybrid work reducing print volumes, which the company addresses by expanding into IT Solutions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tariffs and component costs are material to cash flow: tariff costs rose in 2025, the 2026 gross margin includes a one-time benefit of USD 105 million from tariff refunds whose receivable was sold for about USD 80 million, and the company tied the goodwill impairment to memory price increases and macro uncertainty, so input costs and trade policy move margins and liquidity together. Other political, social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the supplied materials beyond the structural decline in print volumes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are a recurring post sale base, proven cost delivery, lower payouts and liquidity through 2027. Weaknesses are the 2028 to 2030 maturity wall, thin underlying EBITDA against heavy interest, weak free cash flow and an equity deficit. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are delivery of the synergy target and an exchange that reduces debt and extends maturities; threats that could weaken it are further input cost increases, a lowered cash flow outlook and more priority-shifting financings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are recurring revenue, cost delivery and near-term liquidity; the constraints are leverage, interest burden, weak free cash flow and a narrow window to refinance. The trend is mixed: adjusted operating income is improving while the cash flow outlook, receivable sale funding and equity are deteriorating. Missing datapoints are market prices, ratings, covenant headroom and a 2027 cash flow outlook.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are further synergies, savings already reached, lower dividends and an exchange that extends USD 120 million to 2030, and the headwinds are pro forma revenue declines, product cost increases, shrinking receivable sale funding and the lowered operating cash flow outlook of USD 145 million to USD 195 million. Over three to five years the deciding issue is whether EBITDA can be rebuilt toward the level the 2028 to 2030 maturities need before the revolver and the 2028 notes mature; the issuer's own leverage target needs about USD 1,407 million of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is continued pro forma revenue decline of about 5% a year with product cost increases that keep equipment gross margin near the 5.0% of the third quarter. The first operational break is that savings stop covering the decline, so underlying EBITDA stays near USD 416 million or lower instead of rising. The financial transmission is that interest of about USD 357 million leaves little cash, receivable sale proceeds keep falling from USD 122 million in nine months, and operating cash flow stays at or below the low end of the outlook of USD 145 million, so free cash flow is near zero after capital expenditure of USD 94 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 68–69; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidity consequence is gradual rather than abrupt: USD 635 million of cash and revolver availability covers the USD 217 million due through 2027, but revolver availability depends on a borrowing base that shrinks with receivables and inventory, and the revolver matures no later than May 22, 2028, before the USD 556 million of 5.50% notes due in August 2028. The refinancing consequence is that USD 2,931 million due in 2028 to 2030 would have to be refinanced at 10.25% to 13.50% or through more exchanges and asset financings, so unsecured creditors would be asked to accept lower priority. Management levers are the dividend suspension worth about USD 28 million a year, further discounted repurchases, receivable sales and asset-backed financings, and the observable triggers are a further cut to the outlook, falling revolver availability and a failed or delayed exchange. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress before 2028 but not sufficient to refinance the 2028 wall on current earnings without exchanges or asset-backed financing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Xerox Corp presents a weak business profile supported by recurring post sale revenue, cost delivery and scale, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking revenue base, thin one-off-flattered EBITDA, interest that absorbs most of it and USD 2,931 million of maturities in 2028 to 2030. Cash flow durability appears weak because operating cash flow depends on falling receivable sales and the outlook was cut. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovery, the secured debt capacity under the indentures and further asset-backed or priority-shifting transactions. The primary downside path is a refinancing failure at the 2028 wall after the revolver matures. Further analysis would require market prices, ratings, covenant headroom, the amended Term Loan B terms and a 2027 cash flow outlook. Top risk: refinancing of the 2028 to 2030 maturities.
